items.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump
items.description: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia's energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington's ties with war-torn Ukraine. Our correspondent Gulliver Cragg tells us more.

items.title: Can Yemen’s government forces sustain their offensive against the Houthis?
items.description: Houthi missile strikes threaten key supply routes on Yemen's Red Sea coast, intensifying pressure on government forces.

items.title: Oregon school shooting: Police praise 'heroism' of those who intervened to stop more killing
items.description: US police have praised the actions of three people who cut short a deadly shooting at a school in the state of Oregon. Three children and a teacher were killed in the attack, carried out by a former pupil at the school.

items.title: Iran denies Saudi accusation of involvement in Houthi attacks
items.description: Since Yemen's civil war flared back to life in July, the pro-Iran Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.

items.title: A broken peace deal is reigniting war in Ethiopia’s Tigray region
items.description: Issues left unresolved in the peace agreement that ended fighting in Ethiopia’s Tigray region in 2022 are pushing the area once again toward war.

items.title: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role
items.description: The BBC joins Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi as it regains crucial territory in the Donbas, but optimism has been dampened by souring relations with President Trump.

items.title: Kremlin ‘Fully Agrees’ With Trump’s Zelensky Criticism
items.description: Putin continues to demand that Kyiv cede full control of the Donetsk region as a prerequisite for any ceasefire agreement, a condition Ukraine rejects.

items.title: Zelenskyy Says US Diesel Deal Will Put Money 'Straight Into Putin's Pocket'
items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, has no interest in peace talks and criticized a US deal with Moscow on diesel exports, saying it will hand more money to Moscow to fund its war against his country.

items.title: Three years on, Israel still bars foreign journalists from entering Gaza
items.description: More than a year into a declared ceasefire in Gaza — and three years into the war — Israel still hasn't allowed foreign media independent access to Gaza.
